content:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall — sustained spike detected for dedicated-pool-prod-02: 95th latency > 2.1s, error rate (5m) 7.8% (baseline 0.3%), queue depth climbing to 480. Autoretry floods observed. Possible cascading timeouts to backend transformers. Alert triggered at 2026-03-15T14:01:03Z.

alex: oncall here, ack. jumping in — grabbing metrics and checking autoscaler logs now. any known deploys?

maria: I don't see any deploys in the last 30m. Looks like a traffic surge from a subset of API keys — spike originates from eu-west region. High concurrency from a few customers.

samir: checking dedicated autoscaler: pool-02 target_gpus=8 current_gpus=8, scale_up_requests queued but not executed: failed to provision due to capacity error: "insufficient-capacity: region eu-west-1" in infra logs. So autoscaler attempted but cloud couldn't allocate.

alex: ok that explains why scale-up didn't happen. Need live mitigations: options: 1) toggle burst capacity (if any) for pool-02, 2) temporary global rate limiting for low-tier keys, 3) raise per-key quotas for our paying customers impacted, 4) disable non-critical background features (prefetch, embeddings batch jobs). Thoughts?

maria: agree. Prioritize customers with active SLAs: identify impacted enterprise keys and increase quotas for them first. Then open global throttles for free/low-tier to reduce pressure. We'll also enable burst capacity while infra resolves.

jess: tagging customer-success — @natalie-cs flagged two enterprise customers already complaining about 502s. Both are on Dedicated but their traffic funnels through pool-02. They need an ETA and mitigation notes.

alex: quick assessment: impacted customers (~12) experiencing errors on /v1/generate and streaming disconnects. Severity: P1 for 2 enterprise customers, P2 for the rest. Estimated revenue-at-risk: medium.

samir: I can attempt the burst toggle via admin API. Command I'll use (will redact token here):
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/dedicated/pools/pool-02/actions -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"action":"toggle_burst","enable":true,"burst_multiplier":3,"duration_minutes":45}'
```
I'll run this and report status.

alex: while you do that, I'll push a safeguard rate-limit rule for free-tier keys to 20 RPS per key and deprioritize background prefetch. Use the NGW rule set id: rg-kv-03.

maria: we should also set a temporary quota bump for the two P1 customers to prevent throttling on their keys. Samir, can you set per-key override for cust-enterprise-42 and cust-enterprise-07 to 200 RPS?

samir: on it. API call: 
```
POST /admin/keys/cust-enterprise-42/overrides
{ "qps": 200, "expires_at": "2026-03-15T15:00:00Z" }
```
response: 202 Accepted — override queued. Doing the same for cust-enterprise-07.

ops-bot: action-complete: burst-toggle invoked for pool-02, request_id=bt-20260315-008. desired_state=enabled, burst_multiplier=3, expires_at=2026-03-15T14:46:03Z.

samir: cloud provider responded: allocation request succeeded for 4 GPUs burst capacity attached to pool-02. Note: these are "burst" ephemeral nodes with limited lifetime. Pool now reporting current_gpus=12 (8 baseline + 4 burst).

alex: I pushed the NGW rule: free-tier -> 20 RPS per key. Also added a route rule to deprioritize /v1/embeddings/batch and /v1/prefetch to background queue.

maria: customer-success update please, @jess / @natalie-cs — message to customers: brief incident note + steps we took and ask for any time-sensitive traffic you need prioritized.

natalie-cs: sending messages now. For the two P1s: notifying them that we've enabled burst capacity, added per-key overrides, and expect lower error rates in next 4–6 minutes. Offered dedicated support window.

alex: monitoring: within 90s after burst attach, queue depth dropped from 480 -> 120, error rate fell from 7.8% -> 1.8%, 95th latency down to 1.2s. Still above baseline but trending.

maria: nice. We should keep rate limits in place until autoscaler can provision permanent capacity or traffic subsides. Also flag for follow-up: why cloud capacity exhausted — consider pre-warming policy for pool-02 and a larger reserved cap.

samir: creating incident ticket: INC-2026-0315-02 with timeline and actions. Will attach autoscaler and cloud capacity logs.

alex: on-call handoff in 20min — maria will take the next shift and monitor until we close. Maria, please summarize next steps and any on-call playbook additions.

maria: handoff ack. Next steps: 1) keep burst enabled until 15:00 or until autoscaler obtains permanent capacity; 2) maintain free-tier rate limit at 20 RPS; 3) schedule escalation to cloud ops to explain capacity shortfall; 4) postmortem to include: (a) improve pre-warm heuristics for Dedicated pools, (b) add automatic per-key emergency overrides for enterprise SLAs, (c) add a guarded fallback to send non-critical requests to fallback model variants under high load.

alex: noted. I'll prepare short incident summary and assign owners.

ops-bot: monitor-update: 5m rolling — error-rate=1.1%, queue=90, 95th-latency=0.98s. Burst remaining duration 32 minutes.

jess: customers acknowledged messages, two P1s confirm service restoration for most calls but will keep us posted for edge cases.

natalie-cs: capturing impacted customers list and forwarding to eng-ops + account teams.

samir: scheduling a follow-up with cloud provider to request capacity reservation for eu-west-1 for pool-02. Also filing infra change request to raise reserved capacity bound for this pool.

alex: closing notes: mitigation sequence worked — burst attach + targeted per-key overrides + global throttles. Postmortem and runbook updates required. I'll mark this incident as mitigated and handoff to maria to watch for recurrence.

maria: taking over monitoring. If error-rate creeps back above 3% or queue > 200, I'll escalate to on-call pager and attempt further mitigations (extended burst or emergency region failover).

ops-bot: incident-mitigated: status=mitigated, mitigations=[burst_enable, per_key_override, free_tier_rate_limit, deprioritize_prefetch], closed_by=maria, closed_at=2026-03-15T14:16:00Z.

alex: thanks everyone — filing owners for follow-ups: samir (cloud capacity/reservations), maria (runbook updates), jess/natalie-cs (customer communications). Will drop a postmortem draft in #postmortems later today.

maria: thanks. Handoff complete.
